speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for seeing me today. I understand you are experiencing weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm. To help me pinpoint the cause, can you tell me if these symptoms started suddenly or did they develop gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: The progressive weakness and sensory loss in your right arm over a few weeks, combined with significant weight loss and your history of smoking and steroid use, are concerning. Could you describe the specific distribution of the weakness (e.g., hand vs. shoulder) and whether you have experienced any neck pain or numbness radiating down the arm?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast Tumor (Superior Sulcus Tumor) causing Pancoast Syndrome.

Given your history of heavy smoking, significant weight loss, and the specific combination of right arm weakness, sensory loss, and dull burning pain (suggesting brachial plexus involvement), I suspect a lung apex tumor. I need to confirm this with imaging.

REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray.
